drawRectTooltip: Click and drag to draw a rectangle
helpStep1: Draw a selection: click the rectangle icon in the map toolbar (top-right) and drag to mark an area.
helpStep2: Set criteria: use the sliders to control minimum elevation, max slope, peak closeness, valley depth, and peak prominence.
helpStep3: Click "Analyze Area" — terrain data is fetched and analyzed entirely in your browser.
helpStep4: Explore results: directional markers show viewpoints on the map. Click a marker or result card for details.
helpStep5: Save favourites: use ❤️ Love or ⭐ Star buttons to bookmark spots across sessions.
helpStep6: Access warning: viewpoints may be near or on private property. Do not enter private land without permission, and stay on legal public access routes.
helpCreditsMap: Map data and basemaps are provided by OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, and Esri.
helpCreditsGeocoding: Reverse geocoding is provided by OpenStreetMap contributors via Nominatim.

radioClickToBegin: Click on the map to place your transmitter. Right-click or long-press after that to set a direction target.
radioHelpTxAntennaGain: Gain of the transmitting antenna in its main forward direction. This is added to TX power to compute EIRP; it focuses energy rather than creating free power.
radioTxGainUsePattern: Use typical gain from the selected pattern
radioHelpTxGainAuto: Leave this on if you want the app to fill a typical gain for the selected antenna preset. Turn it off if you know the published gain of your actual antenna.
radioTxGainHintPattern: Using the typical gain for {{pattern}}: {{gain}} dBi. Clear this option to enter your own value.
radioTxGainHintNoTypical: This pattern has no typical gain preset. Enter the published or measured antenna gain if you know it.
radioTxGainHintCustom: Manual override. Enter the actual antenna gain if you know it.
radioHelpEngine: Which ITM implementation to use. WASM is usually faster; JavaScript is useful for cross-checking and debugging.
radioHelpPolarization: This is the ITM propagation polarization, separate from the horizontal pattern preset. ITM natively supports vertical and horizontal; 45° slant is approximated as the midpoint between those two model results.
radioHelpClimate: ITM climate class for the average propagation region. If unsure, Continental Temperate is a reasonable inland default.
radioHelpSurfaceRefractivity: Lower-atmosphere refractivity, called N0 in ITM. This affects how much the atmosphere bends radio waves; it is not ground reflectivity.
radioHelpGroundType: Preset electrical properties for the surface between TX and RX. Use Custom only if you know ground permittivity and conductivity.
radioHelpGroundPermittivity: Relative dielectric constant of the ground. Higher values change ground reflection and low-angle propagation.
radioHelpGroundConductivity: Ground conductivity in siemens per meter. Better-conducting ground usually helps low-angle and surface-wave propagation.
radioHelpStatMode: Quick presets for ITM time, location, and situation percentages. Use Custom when you need explicit reliability targets.
radioHelpStatTime: Percentage of time the signal should meet or exceed the prediction. Higher values are more conservative.
radioHelpStatLocation: Percentage of locations within the area that should meet or exceed the prediction. Higher values demand broader area reliability.
radioHelpStatSituation: Percentage of installation and clutter situations that should meet or exceed the prediction. Higher values are more conservative.
radioHelpMdvarBase: Base ITM variability family. Mobile is a sensible default for typical moving or portable links unless you are matching a specific study.
radioHelpMdvarLocationModifier: Adds 10 to mdvar and removes location variability from the model. Use only if you know you want that NTIA variant.
radioHelpMdvarSituationModifier: Adds 20 to mdvar and removes direct situation variability from the model. Use only if you know you want that NTIA variant.
radioHelpResolution: Terrain sampling zoom. Higher zoom gives finer detail but costs more time and memory; Auto picks a reasonable level.
radioHelpRxHeight: Height of the receiving antenna above local ground. Raising RX height often changes coverage more than small power changes.
radioHelpRxGain: Gain of the receiving antenna. This improves received signal level but does not change transmitted power.
radioHelpRxSensitivity: Minimum signal level the receiver needs for usable reception. More negative dBm values mean a more sensitive receiver.
radioHelpPatternPreset: Approximate horizontal antenna pattern used to weight transmit gain by direction. This does not set ITM polarization. Custom lets you upload a 360-line .az file.
radioHelpPatternDirection: Compass bearing of the antenna's main forward lobe. 0° is north, 90° east, 180° south, 270° west.
radioPatternMapHint: You can also drag the bearing handle on the map.
radioHelpSweepMode: Runs the analysis one directional slice at a time. Usually slower, but it reduces request bursts and peak memory pressure.
radioHelpAdaptiveCulling: Skips blocks that are obviously unreachable before running full ITM. Usually faster with little visible accuracy cost.
radioHelpFastFill: When adaptive culling is on, fills uniformly strong blocks without checking every cell. Turn it off for the most conservative per-cell pass.
radioHelpPatternPreview: Quick polar preview of the selected antenna pattern, rotated to the current bearing.
radioDirectionHint: After placing TX, right-click or long-press to set a direction target. The preview sector updates before analysis.
radioHelpAnalysisRadius: Maximum distance to evaluate around the transmitter. Larger radii take more time, memory, and terrain tiles.
radioHelpSectorAngle: Width of the analysis wedge after you set a direction target. Use 360° for an all-around run.
radioTileLimitExceeded: Tile limit exceeded ({{n}} tiles). Try a smaller radius.
radioTileFetchFailed: Failed to load terrain tiles. Check your connection and try again.
radioWasmRequired: Radio Reach requires WebAssembly. Your browser may not support it, or the WASM module failed to load. Open the browser console for details.
radioLowFreqFallbackWarning: ITM is not valid below 20 MHz; results will use free-space approximation only.
radioClampedNotice: (capped at {{km}} km — max possible at this power/frequency)
radioMemoryGuardrail: This run is likely to exceed safe memory limits ({{mb}} MB total, {{bitmapMb}} MB bitmap, about {{ramGb}} GB RAM available). Reduce the area, use sweep mode, or lower the resolution.
radioMemoryWarningSummary: This run is estimated to use about {{totalMb}} MB total ({{bitmapMb}} MB bitmap, {{tileMb}} MB terrain/tile cache).
radioMemoryWarningRam: Detected available memory is about {{ramGb}} GB.
radioMemoryWarningSweep: Sweep mode is off, so the full coverage bitmap stays resident at once and large runs may crash the tab.
radioMemoryWarningManualZoom: A manual zoom was selected, so the auto downscaling guard is bypassed for this run.
